tagline.text: A central Luzon mountain range with Dalton Pass and Imugan Falls

location.label: Location
location.text: Across Nueva Vizcaya, Nueva Ecija and Quirino, centered on Santa Fe

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–4,000 (excluding round-trip transport from Manila, for 2 days and 1 night)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) — 6–7 hours overland

children.text: The Caraballo Mountains are a range in central Luzon between the Sierra Madre and the Cordillera Central, and the place where the Cagayan River begins. You can combine Dalton Pass in Santa Fe, Imugan Falls and Mount Palali into a two-day mountain trip.

The Caraballo Mountains are a mountain range in central Luzon, Philippines. Acting as a bridge between the Cordillera Central to the west and the Sierra Madre to the east, the range spans three provinces: Nueva Ecija, Nueva Vizcaya and Quirino. According to Wikipedia, it is about
54km
long from north to south, about
24km

wide, and covers roughly 1,300 sq km. The range is the source of the Cagayan River, the longest in the Philippines, and is also known as a place where the boundary between the Philippine Plate and the Sunda Plate runs.

For travelers, the Caraballo Mountains are less a single site than the gateway area through which you cross from Manila into the Cagayan Valley to the north. The easiest base is the town of Santa Fe in Nueva Vizcaya. Santa Fe is a highland town at an average elevation of about
, roughly
309km
from Manila and about
53km

from the provincial capital, Bayombong. Around the town you will find the Dalton Pass (Balete Pass) National Shrine, the war memorials at Salacsac Pass (Malico) and Imugan Falls. During the Spanish era Santa Fe was an indigenous settlement called Imugan; it began as the Imugan municipal district in 1917, received its present name in 1959 (taken from its patron, Saint Joseph), and became a regular municipality in 1967. In 1923 the road linking Central Luzon with the Cagayan Valley was informally opened, and it later became today's Maharlika Highway. For a long time, then, this town has been a stopover on the route for people and goods traveling between the two regions.

Dalton Pass is the site of the Battle of Balete Pass, in which the US 25th Division and Filipino guerrillas fought Gen. Tomoyuki Yamashita's Japanese forces from late February to May 1945. The pass was renamed Dalton Pass after Brig. Gen. James Dalton, who was killed in May after the fighting ended. Today it has a viewing deck at about
above sea level and memorial markers, and from it you can see the winding Maharlika Highway and the mountain ridges in one sweep.
For those who want more of the mountains, there is Mount Palali (about

) in the town of Quezon, Nueva Vizcaya. Described as the highest peak of the Caraballo Mountains, it is a two-day climb through rainforest and boulder sections to a summit with a view to the west. If you prefer something lighter, there is a short walk to the waterfall in the village of Imugan in Santa Fe. Note, however, that major road construction is under way in this area, so be sure to check road conditions before you set out. The Caraballo Mountains are not a glossy tourist attraction but a place to slowly take in historic sites, mountain villages and fog-covered passes. Lodging and restaurants are limited, so you need to prepare, but it suits anyone looking for a quiet mountain trip within an overnight reach of Manila.
This memorial park sits on a ridge at about

above sea level on the boundary between Nueva Ecija and Nueva Vizcaya. You can see the zigzagging road climbing the mountain and the surrounding peaks, and the park has a regional obelisk, a 25th Division battle marker and a National Historical Commission marker. You can drive right up to the viewing deck.

blocks.title: Traces of the Battle of Balete Pass

children.text: The 25th Division marker records 7,403 Japanese killed and 2,365 casualties for the American division in the battle that lasted from February to May 1945. A memorial to eight Chinese wartime militia members and a Japanese-inscribed marker praying for peace stand alongside, so you can encounter the memories of several nations in one place.

blocks.title: Salacsac Pass and the Malico ridge

children.text: Another World War II battleground at about

above sea level, it has stalls selling coffee and farm produce, a war memorial, and a resort displaying a Sherman tank. On a clear day you can look west to the mountains around Itogon in Benguet and across the Central Luzon plains. Pangasinan and Nueva Vizcaya are in a boundary dispute over this area, so maps may label it differently.
A two-tier waterfall reached by walking about
1km
in from the village of Imugan in Santa Fe, it is about
(35 feet) high. You can swim in the shallow pool, and the path is paved, so it is not demanding. A guide is not required.
This mountain of about

starts from Barangay Maddiangat in the town of Quezon. The route passes a large-boulder viewpoint called Haring Bato and a campsite near the summit; because the trail is slippery and rain is frequent, it is described as moderately to highly difficult. It is safest to climb with a local guide.

blocks.title: The mountains where the Cagayan River begins

children.text: The Cagayan River, known as the longest river in the Philippines, begins in this range. The valleys and ridges you see between the passes are the terrain where that river's waters start. The Casecnan Protected Landscape and the Pantabangan–Carranglan Watershed Forest Reserve, both protected forest areas, extend across the range.

Every March, Santa Fe holds a festival that promotes the culture of the indigenous Kalanguya people. Events include dance competitions, float parades, and traditional games such as arm wrestling and pig catching, and it is sometimes held around the Dalton Pass shrine. The schedule changes every year, so check announcements from the town hall.
Take an overnight bus from Manila toward the Cagayan Valley. Tell the conductor in advance that you are getting off in Santa Fe.
You arrive in Santa Fe around
in the early morning. Warm up with a hot soup at a roadside eatery.
Take a tricycle to the village of Imugan, register at the barangay hall, and walk to the waterfall.
Swim at the falls, then have lunch at a shop in Imugan village.
Return to the town center to rest, then head up to the Dalton Pass viewpoint in the afternoon to see the scenery before sunset.
Transport back from Imugan to town is limited, so it is safer to ask your tricycle driver in advance to wait or come back to pick you up.

items.title: Day 2
items.subtitle: Salacsac Pass and the trip home

children.text: If you have a vehicle, drive up the Malico road to Salacsac Pass to see the view and the war memorial.
Come down to town, have lunch, and take a bus back to Manila.
If you want to hike, add a day and change the plan to climb Mount Palali from the Bayombong–Solano side.
Take an overnight bus toward the Cagayan Valley (Isabela or Cagayan) and get off in Santa Fe. The trip takes about
6–7 hours
According to reviews from around 2020, the fare was about ₱285. It may have risen since, so check with the bus company.

For Mount Palali, get off at Solano and head to Barangay Maddiangat in the town of Quezon. As of 2012 the fare to Solano was about ₱338, and there are records of late-night departures from Victory Liner's Kamias terminal.
Bus schedules and fares change often. Check the latest departure times before you go.
Santa Fe is about
309km
from Manila. The mountain sections are long and have fog and rockfalls, so an SUV or four-wheel-drive vehicle is recommended.
The Dalton Pass viewpoint is described as about 20–30 minutes by car from Santa Fe.
From the main road in Santa Fe to the village of Imugan, reviews mention a tricycle ride of about
10 minutes
at about ₱50 per person one way. There are also records of a jeepney to Imugan from the waiting shed in front of the town hall, but check the schedule locally.
For Mount Palali, the ride from Solano to Maddiangat takes about
30 minutes
by tricycle or jeep, and reviews mention about ₱150 for a tricycle.
Daytime highs in Santa Fe are reported at about
and nighttime lows at about
. At this elevation it is cooler than Manila, and mornings and evenings are chilly.

Annual rainfall is about 897 mm, with the most falling from June to September. Rain increases rockfalls on mountain roads, thick fog and slippery waterfall trails, so the dry season is recommended. The Kalanguya Festival takes place in March.

and may vary with local conditions.

Along the main road, Santa Fe has a string of grill eateries and simple restaurants. Wikivoyage lists places such as Erel's Ihaw (about ₱100–200) and Jerry's Belihaws (about ₱200–400). Near Imugan Falls there is a small factory that makes fruit spreads, and visitors are said to be able to watch production and buy products.

Lodging choices are few. Wikivoyage lists only Omallio's Homestay in Malico, and the place with more options is the provincial capital, Bayombong. During peak season or festivals, contact your lodging in advance.

On mountain village trips, restaurants often close early. Before heading up to Imugan Falls or Dalton Pass, it is convenient to buy water, snacks and a packed lunch in town. In the cool highlands, hot soups and charcoal-grilled dishes suit the weather, and tasting the coffee and local vegetables sold at roadside stalls is part of the fun. Check prices and opening hours locally.
Before boarding, tell the staff that you are getting off in Santa Fe, and bring a warm jacket for an early-morning arrival.
Transport back from Imugan is scarce, so arrange a round trip or a waiting tricycle with your driver in advance.
The waterfall path can be slippery with stones and mud, so wear shoes with good grip.
Fog often covers Dalton Pass and Salacsac Pass, so going up during clear morning hours gives better views.
Mobile signal can drop out in the mountain sections, so download offline maps.
Bring plenty of cash. ATMs and card payments are rare.
Road construction is under way, so check the latest traffic conditions before you travel.
The Dalton Pass viewpoint is described as having shaded cabanas and a comfort room. Check their condition locally.
Mountain roads often see landslides, rockfalls and thick fog, and the area lies on the Philippine Fault, so adjust your plans in the rainy season and in bad weather.
Construction of the Dalton Pass East Alignment Road and its twin tunnels (scheduled for 2026–2031) is under way, so terrain and traffic may change.
Pangasinan and Nueva Vizcaya are in a boundary dispute over the Malico area, so maps and signs may differ.
Climbing Mount Palali involves heavy rain and slippery trails, so always climb with a guide and bring camping gear.
Some areas are the land of the indigenous Kalanguya communities. Be respectful when taking photos or entering villages.
This is a mountain region where hospitals and pharmacies are far away, so bring basic medicines and water.
The capital of Nueva Vizcaya, about
53km
from Santa Fe. It has more lodging and restaurants, making it a good base.
A riverside gorge park in Nueva Ecija, a good pairing with the southern foothills of the Caraballo Mountains.
A pass in Aritao with a memorial built by Japan's Rakunsankai Society, worth combining with Dalton Pass.
Cross the Sierra Madre to the east of the range and you reach this coastal town in Aurora, known for surfing.
